clips.title: The Unintended Consequences of Measuring Things
clips.why: The cobra effect and Goodhart's law in under two minutes: what happens when one number becomes the goal.
look: The cobra story: a reward for one number that made the real problem worse.
Goodhart's law: when a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure.
Ask yourself what people (or agents) would do if merged PRs per week were the only number on the delivery dashboard.
clips.after: That is why merged PRs never appear without change failure next to them: the partner number makes it hard to game the first one.

clips.title: Understanding Dashboards in Grafana | Panels, Visualizations, Queries, and Transformations
clips.why: Grafana's own explanation of a panel: a query plus a way to draw its result.
look: A panel holds one or more queries, and each query can become its own line.
The query runs against a data source; ours are VictoriaMetrics for numbers and VictoriaLogs for events.
Think of the delivery panel: two queries, merged PRs and change failure, drawn in one picture.
clips.after: Every panel in our four dashboards is this: one or two queries over the series the collector and the nightly job write, drawn so the partner number is always in view.

clips.title: Deep Dive - Time Series Panel Visualizations: What Are They? How to Get Started? | Grafana
clips.why: How to change the look of one series in a panel without touching the others, which is how the change-failure line gets its own axis.
look: Overrides: settings that apply to one series, chosen by its name.
Watch which settings an override can change, such as the unit and the axis.
Compare it with the override in the delivery panel's JSON: byName "change failure %", axis on the right, unit percent.
clips.after: In our dashboards the override lives in the JSON file in git, so the right axis for change failure is reviewed like any other code.

clips.title: FinOps - Budget Forecasting - Predictive Budget Trends - Budget and Forecast Season
clips.why: How cloud cost teams set budgets, thresholds and forecasts, the same thinking as our burn-rate alert.
look: A budget becomes useful when it has thresholds that warn before the money is gone.
Forecasting from the current trend: where the month ends if nothing changes.
Notice that the thresholds lead to people looking, not to services being switched off.
clips.after: Our spend alert is a forecast with a margin: more than 25% above the even line for six hours, and then a person decides. It never stops an agent.

practice.q: Finish the even line: what a scope should have spent by today if it spends its budget evenly.
practice.hint: A built-in function, the partner of day_of_month().
practice.why: Budget times the share of the month that has passed: day 10 of 30 means a third of the budget.

practice.q: Nova's budget is $3,000. On day 6 of a 30-day month it has spent $700. Does the alert warn (more than 25% above the even line)?

options.why: The comparison is with the even line for day 6, not with the whole month's budget.

options.text: Yes: the line is $600, the limit is $750, and $700 is above the line
options.why: Being above the line is not enough. The alert needs more than 1.25 × $600 = $750.

options.text: No: the line is $600 and the limit $750, so $700 is ahead but inside the margin
options.why: $700 is about 17% ahead of the even pace. The 25% margin keeps early-month noise like this quiet.

practice.q: The cache-read share of the CI fixer fell from 85% to 40% overnight, and its cost doubled. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: Something now changes the start of its prompt on every turn, such as a timestamp near the top
options.why: The cache only reuses a prompt start that is exactly the same. A changing timestamp, tool list or model breaks it.

options.text: It reads more files, so it uses more input tokens
options.why: More file reads add tokens, but the stable start of the prompt is still served from the cache, so the share stays high.

options.text: The gateway stopped counting cache reads
options.why: Then the cost would not double. The cost rise says the tokens really are being paid at the full price.

practice.q: Put the life of the spend alert in order, from the nightly job to a decision.
items: The nightly job writes month-to-date spend and budget for each scope
Every hour, the rule compares each scope with 1.25 times its even line
Nova stays above the limit for six hours in a row
The alert posts in #ai-agents-alerts with the agents and teams that grew most
Sean and Nir look at the spend dashboard and decide what to change
practice.why: The rule only warns. Nothing pauses an agent; people decide with the dashboard in front of them.

practice.q: Which panel would you refuse in a review of delivery-impact.json?

options.text: Review wait p50 and p85 per team, with the baseline line
options.why: That is a team number next to its baseline: exactly what the dashboard is for.

options.text: Merged PRs per week for the selected team, on its own
options.why: Throughput alone rewards the wrong thing. It belongs on one panel with change failure.

options.text: Hours main stayed red per week
options.why: A team-level number about main, not about people. It is one of the planned panels.
